content.title: About
content.content: Potato sticks shaped like fries are crunchy snack sticks made from selected potatoes, cut into thin strips and deep‑fried until golden. They have a light salty flavor and a pleasant texture, perfect as a snack or a side to other dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato sticks first appeared in the United States in the 1950s as an alternative to traditional chips.
The fry shape allows more even frying, resulting in a crispier product.
A small amount of food coloring or spices such as paprika is often added to achieve a golden hue.
In many countries the sticks are served with cheese, barbecue or garlic sauces.
Manufacturers often add a modest amount of vegetable oil to improve taste and texture.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Potato sticks provide quickly digestible carbs that give an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Some vitamin C survives the cooking process, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, important for heart and muscle function.

items.title: Low protein content
items.content: While protein is modest, the sticks can complement a balanced diet when paired with other foods.

items.title: Satiety satisfaction
items.content: The crunchy texture and salty taste help promote a feeling of fullness, potentially reducing overeating.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: Excessive salt may raise blood pressure, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Fried sticks are relatively calorie‑dense, which can contribute to weight gain if eaten in large amounts.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Certain vegetable oils used for frying can generate trans fats, which are harmful to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to potatoes or to additives used in processing.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Potato sticks can be enjoyed straight from the bag, dipped in sauces such as ketchup, cheese or barbecue, or used as a crunchy side for meat and fish dishes. They store well in packets or boxes and can be briefly reheated in the oven to restore crispness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sticks in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Properly stored, they remain crisp and flavorful for up to 3 months. Discard any sticks that develop a rancid smell or off‑taste.
